title: Timms says Pip review being published today will ‘rehumanise’ benefit – UK politics live
summary: Some recommendations expected to clash with those of Milburn’s recent report into Neets

blocks.text:
Some recommendations expected to clash with those of Milburn’s recent report into Neets

  • UK disability benefit cuts ‘risk worsening youth destitution’

Libby Brooks has a good explainer about Pip in her First Edition newsletter today. She sets out how Pip was created by the coalition government in response to a “culture war” over benefits, and she describes how the Timms review and the Alan Miliburn review have been at odds.

Here is an extract.

Last week’s Milburn review called for Pip to be scrapped for younger claimants, and for the health element of universal credit to be replaced by an additional cost allowance, part of a wider network of job-based help for this age group.

The shock among the organisations which had contributed to Timms was palpable, says Patrick [Butler, the Guardian’s social affairs editor]. “The idea that you basically blow up Pip for younger people took a lot of groups by surprise.”

Sporting organisations will be required to demonstrate “structural equality” to receive public funding as part of the drive, the government said.

Officials said the ambition would take into account how women and girls show up in viewing figures, coaching positions and on boards, as well as seeking to ensure they have the same access as boys to sports like football and rugby in school.
